title: A default gather resolves the read job and travels under the winning name
action:
RED FIRST (bugfix playbook). In prepare.rs's test module add a test that a host configured `{"models":{"claude":{"read":"haiku","generation":"sonnet","review":"opus"}}}` gets, for `envelope(&root, "gather", None)`, `payload.model == "haiku"`, `payload.subagent_type == "bee-gather"`, the prompt opening `[bee-tier: read]` and `economics.logical_tier == "read"`; run `cargo test ... prepare` and watch it fail because the envelope says sonnet/generation. Then make it green, per D1-D3:

(1) `slot_for_kind` in prepare.rs — the arm reading `"cell" | "gather" => Some("generation"),` (rg hit prepare.rs:57) splits: `"cell" => Some("generation")`, `"gather" => Some("read")`. Update the pinned test `assert_eq!(slot_for_kind("gather"), Some("generation"));` (rg hit prepare.rs:2923) to `Some("read")`.

(2) `tier_role_list` in models.rs — the body `if slot == "review" { return vec![slot, "generation"]; }` (rg hit models.rs:655) gains a second rule: `read` walks `[read, generation]`. NOT through `extraction`: extraction was the tier-era cheapest slot and never the gather slot, so a legacy host that configures `extraction` + `generation` (the THREE_SLOTS fixture at prepare.rs:2996 is exactly that host) must keep its gathers on `generation` byte-for-byte — say so in the doc comment, citing 561e1bda's tail rule. Leave `cell_role_list("read")` (`if role == "read" { &["extraction", "generation"] }`, rg hit prepare.rs:362) untouched: a read-shaped CELL is a backfilled `tier: extraction` cell (doctrine B8) and its tail is honest as it stands; add one sentence to its doc comment naming why the two read lists differ.

(3) The winner travels on the default-gather path (D2). At the resolve block — rg hits prepare.rs:1452 `if from_role { cell_role_list(tier_token) } else { tier_role_list(tier_token) };` and prepare.rs:1454 `if from_role {` — widen the winner record to `from_role || (kind == "gather" && role.is_none())` (use whatever local already says an explicit --role was passed), and extend the comment above `let mut resolved_role` ("Set only on the cell-role path…") with the reason: `read` is not in `default_models("claude")`, so a marker saying `read` on a host with no `read` key names nothing the guard knows. Every OTHER path keeps today's marker bytes — assert in a test that `--kind reviewer` on a host with no `review` key is byte-identical to today (`[bee-tier: review]`, `subagent_type: bee-review`). Keep `tier_source` as it is (`default`).

(3b) D7 — the bare-dispatch FIX. In model_guard.rs `bare_dispatch_denied`, both format strings (rg hits model_guard.rs:1120 and :1132, `"FIX: name one of bee's rendered agents in subagent_type (bee-gather = generation, \`) lead with `run ".bee/bin/bee dispatch prepare --runtime claude --kind <cell|gather|reviewer|advisor> --json" — it reads .bee/config.json and returns the tool and exact payload` as the FIRST remedy; the rendered-agent sentence that follows is built from `crate::verbs::drivers::ROLE_AGENTS` (agent name + the one-clause purpose the guard already keys on agent), never retyped as `bee-gather = generation`. Drop the hard-coded `--kind gather` literal in the second branch in favour of the generic `<kind>` form. Update the test at model_guard.rs:1794 `assert!(stderr.contains("bee-gather = generation"), "the FIX teaches the new route");` to assert the FIX opens with `dispatch prepare` and names `bee-gather` without the `= generation` pairing. Deny codes and verdicts are byte-identical.

(4) The agent comes from the ASKED name and the kind, never the winner (D3). At `let pinned_type = if kind == "cell" { "bee-build" } else { pinned_agent_type(marker_role) };` (rg hit prepare.rs:1533) add the middle arm: a `--kind gather` dispatch with NO `--role` pins `bee-gather` whichever spelling won (without the pin, a `read` winner would answer `bee-extract` through the read→extraction alias); every other dispatch keeps `pinned_agent_type(marker_role)` exactly as today — on those paths marker_role is still the asked token, so `--role extraction` stays `bee-extract` (doctrine B11; the test `every_rendered_agent_is_reachable_through_the_one_door` at prepare.rs:3038 pins it) and `--kind reviewer` stays `bee-review`. Write the condition with the same explicit-role local as step (3).

(4b) D8 — the fallback contract keys on the winner, both halves. Prepare: at the herding arm `if let Some(model) = CONFIGURABLE_SLOTS` / `.contains(&marker_role)` / `.then(|| default_models(runtime).get(marker_role).cloned())` (rg hits prepare.rs:1741-1743) nothing changes in code — marker_role is now the winner on the gather path — but ADD the test: `read: {kind:"herding", agent:"x", fallback:"default"}` publishes NO `payload.fallback` (read has no built-in default, same as advisor; say so in the comment above), and no-`read` + `generation: {kind:"herding", fallback:"default"}` still publishes `sonnet`. Guard: in `configured_model_set` (model_guard.rs, the loop opening `for kind in crate::verbs::drivers::DISPATCH_KINDS {` / `let Some(slot) = crate::verbs::drivers::slot_for_kind(kind) else { continue };`, rg hit model_guard.rs:608-609) replace the head-slot resolve with `resolve_role_named(models, &tier_role_list(slot), "claude", GUARD_PURPOSE)` and look the default up by the name that WON, so a host with no `read` key and a herding-with-default `generation` keeps admitting `sonnet`; add that test (an Agent dispatch with `model: "sonnet"` and no marker on such a host is allowed, not `param-not-configured`). Rewrite the comment above the loop ("the day slot_for_kind can reach the extraction role…") to describe the walk.

(5) The guard's FIX keeps its kind and names the role. `dispatch_kind_for_role` in model_guard.rs (rg hit model_guard.rs:778-783, `.find(|kind| crate::verbs::drivers::slot_for_kind(kind) == Some(role))`) must answer `gather` for BOTH `read` and `generation`: match a role against `tier_role_list(slot_for_kind(kind))` rather than the head alone. `generation` sits in both the gather and reviewer lists; `DISPATCH_KINDS` order (`cell` filtered, then `gather` before `reviewer`) is what makes it answer `gather` — pin that order in the test at model_guard.rs:2684 `assert_eq!(dispatch_kind_for_role("generation"), Some("gather"));` and add `read` → `gather`; keep `extraction` → `None` (the test `a_herding_shaped_extraction_slot_denies_bee_extract_without_a_wrong_kind` at model_guard.rs:1848 pins that). Every FIX string that renders the kind (the `match dispatch_kind_for_role(t)` sites — rg hits model_guard.rs:937, :997, :1022, :1060, :1085) appends `--role {t}` after `--kind {kind}`, so on a split host (`read: sonnet`, `generation: {kind:herding}`) a `[bee-tier: generation]` refusal names a door that resolves generation, not the read head. Update the tests that pin those FIX bytes to expect the `--role` form.

(6) Fix every test the move turns red honestly — `absent_role_every_dispatch_is_byte_identical` (prepare.rs:3088, `("gather", "bee-gather", "sonnet")`) stays green unchanged because THREE_SLOTS has no `read` key; if it goes red, the walk is wrong, not the test. Add tests for: `read: {kind:"herding", agent:"x"}` → `tool == "Bash"`, command contains `--agent "x"`, `logical_tier == "read"`; `read: null` + `generation: sonnet` → `generation` wins and `subagent_type == "bee-gather"`; `--kind gather --role extraction` still returns `bee-extract`.

(7) Live proof at cap (plan.md test matrix, last row): from the MAIN checkout (/home/thanhsmind/Projects/goglbe/beehive — `dispatch prepare` refuses inside a worktree) drive the freshly built binary against a scratch onboarded host whose `.bee/config.json` sets `models.claude.read: "haiku", generation: "sonnet"` — the verify-app skill's sandbox recipe shows how to make one — and record on the cap: `dispatch prepare --runtime claude --kind gather --json` → `bee-gather`/`haiku`/`[bee-tier: read]`; `--kind reviewer --json` → `bee-review`; then with `read: {kind:"herding", agent:"x"}` → `tool: Bash`. Record the three envelopes' key lines as the `green:live` proof segment. Cell role is `code`; keep the tests inline in the files you touch and cite decision 295f3d03 for the contract they pin.

truths: On a host with read: haiku, generation: sonnet, `dispatch prepare --kind gather` returns bee-gather on haiku with marker [bee-tier: read] and logical_tier read
On a host with no read key (extraction+generation+review), the gather envelope is byte-identical to before the change
On a host with read: {kind: herding}, a default gather returns the Bash herding command
dispatch_kind_for_role answers gather for both read and generation, None for extraction
On a host with no review key, --kind reviewer is byte-identical to today (bee-review, [bee-tier: review])
read: {kind: herding, fallback: default} publishes no payload.fallback; no-read + generation herding-with-default still publishes and admits sonnet on both doors
A bare Agent dispatch's FIX opens with bee dispatch prepare and never says bee-gather = generation

artifacts.substantive: gather slot = read; kind-pinned bee-gather for the default gather; winner recorded on the non-cell path; red-then-green tests
tier_role_list(read) = [read, generation] with the doc comment naming why extraction is not in the tail

key_links: model_guard::dispatch_kind_for_role reads tier_role_list(slot_for_kind(kind)) so the FIX text still names --kind gather for generation
prohibitions: No change to ROLE_AGENTS, ROLE_ALIASES, role_for_agent, agents_for_role (D4)
No change to any deny code or verdict in model_guard.rs
No change to the advisor, reviewer, or cell resolution paths

trace.outcome: A default gather resolves the read slot, travels under the winning name, and keeps bee-gather; the guard mirrors the walk on both halves of the fallback contract
deviations: The guard's fallback default is keyed on the name PREPARE travels under (the winner on the gather kind, the asked head elsewhere) instead of the winner on every kind — a winner-on-every-kind lookup makes the guard NARROWER than prepare on a null-review + herding-generation host, where prepare publishes opus off marker_role and the existing test an_explicitly_null_review_slot_inherits_the_generation_herding_fallback pins that opus stays admitted — the plan was wrong about a fact

The cell's verify command `cargo test ... prepare model_guard drivers` is rejected by cargo (`unexpected argument 'model_guard'`); ran it as `cargo test ... -- prepare model_guard drivers` so libtest takes all three filters, and then ran the whole crate suite as well — hit an unforeseen obstacle

Renamed the pinned test every_dispatch_kind_keeps_its_slot to every_dispatch_kind_names_its_slot_explicitly — 'keeps its slot' became a lie for gather the moment the arm split, and a test name that misdescribes its own assertion is the next reader's wrong turn — found a better route

mistakes.wrong: Asserted model == "sonnet" in a_review_less_host_keeps_its_reviewer_envelope_byte_for_byte after reading resolve_role_named's walk alone
mistakes.better: should have read normalize_models first: it overlays claude's built-in review: opus, so a review-less host never reaches the generation tail and the honest golden is opus
